title: Every release-gated HTTP endpoint must declare a latency SLO and stay within it under nominal load
statement: Every non-public endpoint implemented by STYNX and not present on the bootstrap allow-list MUST declare latency SLOs covering at least p50 and p95. The SLO may be declared in a use-case acceptance criterion, a sibling `*.slo.json` file under `docs/performance/`, or the repository test policy. Defaults are p50 < 200ms and p95 < 800ms for reads, and p50 < 500ms and p95 < 2000ms for writes. Exceeding the declared p95 under nominal-load probes or `pnpm test:perf` is release-gating. Prospective publication of exactly STYNX 1.6.0 is separately scoped by ADR-RELEASE-0001 and law/policy/release-scope-1.6.0.json: no HTTP/k6 nominal-load observation is required for that one publication. Such missing measurements remain NOT_OBSERVED or UNKNOWN, never PASS or N/A; all SLOs, comparison thresholds, populations and future performance qualification obligations remain unchanged. The existing cold-unit pnpm test:perf task remains required with its unchanged policy.
rationale: Stynx surfaces dedicated `/_probes/*` endpoints (data-tx, idempotency, ratelimit, readonly-write) as a built-in performance smoke surface, but pre-Phase-30 no invariant referenced them — `sense-spec-performance-targets` (Phase 27.D) flagged stynx with FAIL on F1×T7 because the spec layer carried zero perf-typed invariants. This invariant promotes a baseline gate: endpoints inherit pack defaults if they don't author per-endpoint SLOs, so initial adopters get measured-and-graded performance for free. Adopters with stricter requirements override per-endpoint via `*.slo.json`. The 'gate' severity is conservative for an initial promotion — the actual enforcement triggers only when `sense-perf-test` produces SR readings (post-Phase-30.H ships the sensor); pre-30.H the invariant is structurally present but un-measurable, mirroring INV-RBAC-001's pre-Phase-22 stance.

strategy.rationale: Executable repository tests and structural trace verification deterministically enforce this established STYNX behavior.
